title: UPDATE: Volta's $5B AI Debt Prices at 11.4% Yield After Banks Limit Risk

tickers.name: CoreWeave, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Lead managers have closed the books on a large-scale debt sale to fund GPU capacity, securing a yield that compensates for elevated sector risks. The financing for Volta Infrastructure’s expansion priced at 11.4% yield to maturity for a total of $5 billion, though JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs restricted their underwriting to a $1.3 billion lease-support loan and left the remaining $3.7 billion tranche as an uncommitted sale.

The loan is unrated and supported by a six-year compute agreement with Anthropic, a structure that limited access to buyers of traditional collateralized loan obligations. This appetite for higher premiums has appeared across the sector, with CoreWeave's recent $2.6 billion facility pricing at SOFR plus 550 basis points, compared to initial indications of 425 to 450 basis points.

selectedTweets.text:
Funding terms are getting more expensive it seems on broader market concerns. 

Apparently, Volta is marketing ~$5bn of AI infrastructure debt at ~11%(!), with a six-year Anthropic compute agreement behind the project. JPMorgan/Goldman have underwritten the $1.3bn lease-support loan, while the $3.7bn GPU tranche is being sold without their underwriting commitment. The deal is also unrated, limiting access to the CLO buyers that normally absorb leveraged loans.

CoreWeave’s $2.6bn facility needed SOFR+550bp versus initial talk of +425–450bp, and an issue price of 97 versus 99. Its roughly five-year debt finances customer contracts averaging three years, leaving lenders exposed to whether that capacity can be re-leased. The spread increase alone adds ~$26–33m/year if fully drawn.

SoftBank’s September dollar bonds cost 8.625–9.75%. Across the $10bn raised, that is roughly $941m in annual coupons.
